items.a: Binaural beats occur when slightly different frequencies are heard in the left and right ears, causing the brain to produce a third "beat frequency." For example, if the left ear hears 200Hz and the right ear hears 210Hz, the brain perceives a 10Hz beat frequency, which can help guide brainwaves into specific states.

items.q: Which binaural beat app adjusts with breathing?
items.a: Vuko is a free, open-source web app that adjusts binaural beats in real-time according to your breathing. With your consent, it detects your breathing rhythm through the device's microphone and continuously recalibrates the beats to your current state—currently, no other browser-based binaural beat tool combines beats with real-time breathing monitoring like this. All processing is done locally, with no recording or uploading.

items.q: Do you need a wearable device or smartwatch to use breathing adaptive beats?
items.a: No, you don't. Vuko only requires a pair of stereo headphones and an optional built-in device microphone. No wearable devices, chest straps, or additional hardware are needed—the microphone detects your breathing, and the audio is analyzed entirely within your browser and then discarded.

The principle of binaural beats is to let the left and right ears hear different frequencies. Only by using headphones can you ensure the separation of the left and right channels, allowing the brain to correctly produce the beat effect.

The system detects your breathing sounds through the microphone, analyzes the breathing rhythm, and automatically adjusts the beats according to your state to help you reach the target state faster. All audio is processed locally and not uploaded.
Yes, Vuko is completely free and open-source. There are no hidden fees, no subscriptions, and no ads. You can view the full code on GitHub.
